subject.title: feat(skills): add option to disable ~/.agents/skills scanning for Claude Code coexistence

question: What public `skills.load` contract should OpenClaw expose for disabling built-in skill sources such as `agents-skills-personal`?
rationale: The source-level issue is clear, but adding a config knob changes OpenClaw's public configuration surface and built-in skill discovery semantics, which repository policy treats as a maintainer product decision.

options.title: Typed source-disable list
options.body: Add a backward-compatible typed list such as `skills.load.disableSources` covering discovery, watcher registration, status/docs, and tests while preserving current defaults when unset.

options.title: Narrow personal-source toggle
options.body: Add only a boolean opt-out for `~/.agents/skills`, reducing surface area but making future source controls less uniform.

options.title: No config knob
options.body: Keep current cross-agent discovery as mandatory and document per-skill disables or allowlists as the supported workaround.

recommendation.title: Typed source-disable list
recommendation.body: Add a backward-compatible typed list such as `skills.load.disableSources` covering discovery, watcher registration, status/docs, and tests while preserving current defaults when unset.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent skills/config routing points to this owner for the current surface, while the decision is product/config policy rather than only the original discovery patch.
